facts.text: Fancy Gap takes its name from a natural pass through the Blue Ridge Mountains that travelers have crossed for centuries.
The gap sits at roughly 2,900 feet elevation, marking a climate and vegetation transition while still being a practical mountain route.
Native American trails once followed this route, later becoming a stagecoach road whose remnants can still be seen in Devil’s Den Nature Preserve.
Fancy Gap is an unincorporated community of residences, small businesses, and rural properties spread along ridges and hollows near the gap.
The community sits near the North Carolina line, where the Blue Ridge escarpment drops sharply to the east and a gentle high plateau rises to the west.
